# Quotas (/requests/quotas)

A quota limits how many requests a user can make in a period. Requests over the limit wait in the [approval queue](/requests/approval-queue). A watchlist cap skips new watchlist items past the cap instead of requesting them. Skipped items are not held for approval.

## Set a user's quota [#set-a-users-quota]

Open a user from **Users** > **Plex users**. Movies and shows have separate quotas. To set quotas for several users at once, select them on **Plex users** and use **Edit quotas**. New users get the quotas set on [New user defaults](/users/new-user-defaults).

- **Limit requests** turns the quota on.
- **Quota period** is **Daily**, **Weekly rolling** or **Monthly**.
- **Requests per period** is the limit.
- **Bypass approval over the limit** sends requests over the limit straight through, and turns the cap off.
- **Cap the watchlist** and **Watchlist cap** skip new watchlist items past the cap. These fields show only while **Limit requests** is on.

**Remove quotas** deletes the user's quotas and caps. It can also approve the requests their quota was holding.

## How periods reset [#how-periods-reset]

- **Daily** resets at midnight, server time.
- **Weekly rolling** counts the requests from the last few days, today included. A request stops counting once it's older than the window.
- **Monthly** resets at midnight, server time, on the day you choose.

Set the weekly window and the monthly reset day under **Requests** > **Quotas**:

- **Count requests from the last** is the weekly rolling window, in days.
- **Reset on day** is the monthly reset day.
- **When a month is too short** only matters for a reset day of the 29th or later. **Reset on the last day** resets on the month's last day, **Skip that month** waits for the next reset, and **Reset on the 1st** resets on the 1st of the following month.

To approve held requests automatically once a user's quota resets, turn on **Approve automatically when a quota resets** in [Approval settings](/requests/approval-settings).

## Usage history [#usage-history]

Each request a quota counts is kept as a usage record. **Delete old usage history** removes records older than **Keep usage history for**. Keep them at least as long as your longest quota period, or requests that still count are deleted.

**Quota maintenance** runs that cleanup. **Run on a schedule** turns it on or off, and **Run at** sets the time, in the server's time zone.

## Watchlist cap notifications [#watchlist-cap-notifications]

**Send cap notifications to** picks where admins hear that a user reached their watchlist cap. **Notify the user** also tells the user, by Discord or Apprise if they use them.


# Account (/system/account)

Your admin account is the login for Pulsarr itself, separate from your Plex account. Open **Account settings** from the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar.

- **Profile** has the **Email** and **Username** you sign in with.
- **Password** takes a **New password** and **Confirm new password**. Leave both blank to keep your current one.

Enter your **Current password** under **Confirm changes** to save any of them.

To turn sign-in off, or skip it on your local network, set `authenticationMethod` in [`.env`](/installation/environment-variables#security).


# API keys (/system/api-keys)

An API key lets another app, such as Home Assistant or your own script, call the [Pulsarr API](/api). Manage keys under **System** > **API keys**.

Enter a **Name** that says what will use the key, then select **Create key**. **Copy key** copies it. Send it in the `X-API-Key` header with each request.

A wrong or revoked key gets a 401, even on a network where sign-in is skipped.

**Revoke** cuts off anything using a key straight away, and it can't be undone.


# System (/system)

These pages cover Pulsarr's link to Plex, access to its API, its log and your admin login.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Plex connection" href="/system/plex-connection" description="The Plex account and server, watchlist feeds and library refresh." />
  <Card title="API keys" href="/system/api-keys" description="Let other apps and scripts call the Pulsarr API." />
  <Card title="Logs" href="/system/logs" description="Read the log as it's written, and set how much it records." />
  <Card title="Account" href="/system/account" description="Your admin email, username and password." />
</Cards>


# Logs (/system/logs)

**System** > **Logs** shows Pulsarr's log as it's written. Use **Search lines** and the **Level** filter to find what you need.

Under **Log settings**:

- **Application log level** sets how much Pulsarr records, from **Fatal** to **Trace**, or **Silent** to record nothing. Raise it to **Debug** when you're chasing a problem, and set it back afterwards. A `logLevel` set in [`.env`](/installation/environment-variables) replaces this every time Pulsarr starts.
- **Initial lines** is how many earlier lines load when you open the page.

The log files themselves are in the `logs` folder of Pulsarr's data folder, for example `./data/logs` in Docker.


# Plex connection (/system/plex-connection)

Find these under **System** > **Plex connection**.

## Plex account [#plex-account]

Pulsarr reads watchlists through the Plex account that owns your server. To link a different account, select **Relink with Plex** and approve Pulsarr on plex.tv, or **Paste a token** if you already have one.

**Unlink** removes the account. Watchlist syncing stops until you link again, and your requests and settings stay.

## Plex server [#plex-server]

**Connection** starts on **Automatic**, which lets Pulsarr pick the best connection to your server. Choose **Address** to enter it yourself. **Test connection** checks it.

**Skip content already on Plex** skips requests for titles already on Plex. **Servers to check** sets where Pulsarr looks, **Your server** or **Your server and shared servers**. Shared servers count only for the admin's own watchlist. If your server can't be checked, Pulsarr holds the request and tries again later instead of sending it.

**Plex live connection** shows whether Pulsarr is getting live updates from your server. While it's down, Pulsarr polls Plex instead.

## Watchlist feeds [#watchlist-feeds]

With Plex Pass, Pulsarr watches two RSS feeds, **Your watchlist feed** and **Friends' watchlist feed**, so new watchlist items arrive within seconds. Without Plex Pass, Pulsarr checks each watchlist about every five minutes. **Generate feeds** asks Plex for the feed URLs. **Generate again** asks for new ones and replaces the old ones.

**Sync watchlists** reads your and your friends' watchlists from Plex again.

## Plex library refresh [#plex-library-refresh]

Sonarr and Radarr can tell Plex to refresh its library after they import something. **Set up** adds that Plex Media Server connection to every Sonarr and Radarr instance, and **Remove** takes it off all of them, including ones added by hand.

The Plex connection Pulsarr adds uses the host, port and SSL setting of your **Address**, or of the connection **Automatic** picked. An address without a port gets 443 with SSL and 80 without.


# Users (/users)

Pulsarr adds your Plex friends as users on its own. These pages set what each user can do and mark their requests in Sonarr, Radarr and Plex.

<Cards>
  <Card title="Plex users" href="/users/plex-users" description="Sync, approval, notifications and quotas for each person." />
  <Card title="New user defaults" href="/users/new-user-defaults" description="What users start with when Pulsarr first sees them." />
  <Card title="User tags" href="/users/user-tags" description="Tag content in Sonarr and Radarr by who has it on their watchlist." />
  <Card title="Plex labels" href="/users/plex-labels" description="Label movies and shows in Plex by who has them on their watchlist." />
</Cards>


# New user defaults (/users/new-user-defaults)

Each time Pulsarr syncs, any Plex friend it hasn't seen before becomes a user with these settings. Changing them doesn't affect existing users. Edit those on [Plex users](/users/plex-users). Find these under **Users** > **New user defaults**. You also set them during first-run setup.

Under **Access**:

- **Sync watchlist** is on by default. Turn it off to add new users without requesting what they watchlist.
- **Require approval** holds every request from new users in the [approval queue](/requests/approval-queue).

Under **Movies** and **Shows**, **Limit requests** gives new users a [quota](/requests/quotas) with a **Quota period** and **Requests per period**. **Bypass approval over the limit** sends their requests over the limit straight through and turns the cap off. With **Cap the watchlist** on, new watchlist items past the **Watchlist cap** are skipped instead of requested. The cap fields show only while **Limit requests** is on.


# Plex labels (/users/plex-labels)

Plex labels mark each movie and show in Plex with the users who have it on their watchlist. Set them up under **Users** > **Plex labels**.

## Labeling [#labeling]

**Label content in Plex** labels each item with who watchlists it, once the item is in Plex. A label is the **Prefix** and the user's name, for example `pulsarr:jamie`. **Name from** picks **Username** or **Alias**. Labels also apply when Sonarr or Radarr reports an import to Pulsarr.

The format can't change while Pulsarr's labels exist. Remove them first with **Remove all Pulsarr labels**.

## When something leaves a watchlist [#when-something-leaves-a-watchlist]

**Label behavior** decides what happens to a user's label when they remove the item:

- **Remove the label** removes it.
- **Keep the label** keeps it as a record of who asked.
- **Swap for a removed label** replaces it with the **Removed label** once nobody wants the item, so you can find it.

**Clean up orphaned labels on sync** removes labels for users who were deleted, renamed or stopped syncing. **Reset labels before each sync** applies the rule above to leftover labels before each sync. Turn it on after you move away from **Keep the label**.

## Tag sync [#tag-sync]

**Sync tags as labels** copies Sonarr and Radarr tags to Plex as labels, except user tags. Pulsarr pairs a Plex item with its Sonarr or Radarr entry by file path, so Plex and the arrs must see the media under the same paths. Each tag on an item becomes a label on it, with the same prefix. **Radarr tags on movies** and **Sonarr tags on shows** pick which ones.

## Full sync [#full-sync]

**Full sync** rechecks every watchlisted item and fixes its labels. It needs labeling on. **Run on a schedule** runs it at the time and, if you like, the day of the week set in **Run at**, in the server's time zone.

## Remove labels [#remove-labels]

**Clean up orphaned labels** deletes labels of removed, renamed or non-syncing users. **Remove all Pulsarr labels** strips every label Pulsarr added, user and tag labels alike. Other labels and your content aren't touched.


# Plex users (/users/plex-users)

**Users** > **Plex users** lists you, your Plex friends, and anyone with access to your Plex server. Pulsarr adds friends on its own, with your [new user defaults](/users/new-user-defaults).

The table shows each user's **Relationship**, **Watchlist** size, whether they **Sync**, whether they need **Approval**, their **Notifications** and their **Quotas**. Use **Search users** and the filters to narrow it.

## Relationship [#relationship]

- **Owner** is your own Plex account.
- **Friend** is a Plex friend with access to your server.
- **No server** is a Plex friend without server access. Their requests sync, but they can't watch.
- **No friend** has access to your server but isn't a Plex friend.
- **Pending** is a friend request you sent that they haven't accepted.
- **Incoming** is a friend request they sent you. Accept it in Plex.
- **Managed** is a Plex Home account without a watchlist.

## Not yet friends [#not-yet-friends]

Pulsarr can only read the watchlists of your Plex friends. People it can't track yet show under **Not yet friends**, except **Managed** accounts. Select **Send friend request** for a **No friend** account, or **Cancel request** or **Resend request** for a **Pending** one.

A friend whose **Watchlist** shows 0 may have an empty watchlist or a private one. Pulsarr can't tell which. See the [quick start](/installation/quick-start#before-you-start) for the Plex privacy setting.

## Change one user [#change-one-user]

Select a user to open their page.

- **Identity** shows their **Plex username**, which can't be changed here, and an **Alias** shown instead of it in Pulsarr and notifications.
- **Access** has **Sync watchlist**, which requests what they add, and **Require approval**, which holds their requests in the [approval queue](/requests/approval-queue).
- **Notifications** has their **Discord user ID** and **Apprise URL**, and switches for **Discord**, **Discord mention**, **Apprise** and **Plex mobile**. **Send a test** sends through the channels saved for them.
- **Movies** and **Shows** set their [quota and watchlist cap](/requests/quotas).

The page also shows what's on their watchlist, their requests by status and their quota usage.

**Remove friend** ends the Plex friendship. Their Pulsarr record, watchlist and quotas are deleted at the next sync.

## Change several users [#change-several-users]

Select users in the table, then:

- **Edit settings** changes access and notifications for all of them. Fields left as is keep each user's current value. **Clear values** removes their alias, Discord user ID or Apprise URL.
- **Edit quotas** sets or removes their quotas.


# User tags (/users/user-tags)

User tags mark each movie and show in Sonarr and Radarr with the users who have it on their watchlist. Set them up under **Users** > **User tags**.

## Where to tag [#where-to-tag]

**Tag movies in Radarr** and **Tag shows in Sonarr** add a tag for each user who has the item on their watchlist.

## Tag format [#tag-format]

A tag is the **Prefix** and the user's name, for example `pulsarr-user-jamie`. **Name from** picks **Username** or **Alias**. Users without an alias fall back to their Plex username.

The format can't change while the tags exist in Sonarr or Radarr. Remove them first with **Remove all user tags** and **Also delete the tag definitions**.

## When something leaves a watchlist [#when-something-leaves-a-watchlist]

**Tag behavior** decides what happens to a user's tag when they remove the item:

- **Remove the tag** removes it.
- **Keep the tag** keeps it as a record of who asked.
- **Swap for a removed tag** removes it, and adds the **Removed tag** once nobody wants the item, so you can find it. [Delete sync](/library/delete-sync) in tag based mode deletes content with that tag.

**Clean up orphaned tags on sync** removes the tags of users who were deleted or renamed in Plex.

## Actions [#actions]

- **Sync tags** tags everything currently on a watchlist and clears tags that no longer apply.
- **Create missing tags** adds a tag in each instance for any user who doesn't have one yet.
- **Clean up orphaned tags** deletes tags left behind by users who were removed or renamed.
- **Remove all user tags** strips every user tag from movies and shows. Your content isn't touched. **Also delete the tag definitions** removes the tags themselves from Sonarr and Radarr too.
